subject: Post-signature MAP: rollout criteria, canary plan, migration windows
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.k@hearthwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature MAP: rollout criteria, canary plan, migration windows

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for signing — really excited to get Hearthwave onto Redwood Dedicated. Attached is our initial mutual action plan (HW_MAP_v1.xlsx) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan. High-level items included:

- Rollout phases (Pilot -> Canary -> Production) with acceptance criteria for each phase.
- Canary gating: traffic slice percentages, error thresholds (P95 latency, token error rate), and automatic fallback triggers.
- Migration windows: proposed 3-hour maintenance windows for data sync and cutover (UTC-friendly slots listed).
- Training & handoffs: three 90-minute sessions for engineering + two 60-minute ops runbooks for support.
- Roles & owners: mapping for Hearthwave IT, Redwood deployment lead, and escalation contacts.

Action items for you: please confirm preferred maintenance window(s) (we listed Fri 01:00–04:00 UTC as primary), and whether your Security team needs any additional artifacts before we schedule the canary.

I cc'd Karthik to propose the canary cadence and Marissa for post-close onboarding. If the MAP looks good, we can lock dates and share the Canary checklist (PDF) for your runbook.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: HW_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-canary-checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.k@hearthwave.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hearthwave Procurement <procurement@hearthwave.com>, Hearthwave Security <security@hearthwave.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: rollout criteria, canary plan, migration windows

Evelyn —

Appreciate the fast follow. A couple of clarifications from our side after a quick pass with engineering and security:

1) Maintenance window: Fri 01:00–04:00 UTC works for SRE, but our data team prefers Sun 02:00–05:00 UTC for the final cutover to minimize analytics impact. Can you support both as options?

2) Canary gating: can you confirm whether automatic fallback will route to our existing model endpoints or to a read-only mode? We need to know how failback impacts downstream queues.

3) Security artifacts: security@hearthwave.com asked for: SOC 2 Type II scope, retention and delete-by-request flow, and an on-prem dataflow diagram. Do you have a one-page summary or link we can share with them?

If you can answer the three items above, procurement will proceed with final redlines next week.

Thanks,
Daniel Kim
Senior Director, Platform Engineering
Hearthwave
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.k@hearthwave.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: rollout criteria, canary plan, migration windows

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the notes — answers inline and next steps below. Quoting your points for clarity.

> 1) Maintenance window: Fri 01:00–04:00 UTC works for SRE, but our data team prefers Sun 02:00–05:00 UTC for the final cutover to minimize analytics impact. Can you support both as options?

Yes — we can support both slots. Recommended approach: schedule the pilot and canary during Fri 01:00–04:00 UTC (less risk to analytics because traffic slice is small), and reserve Sun 02:00–05:00 UTC for the final production cutover (full traffic flip). I added both windows in HW_MAP_v1.xlsx (Sheet: Timing).

> 2) Canary gating: can you confirm whether automatic fallback will route to our existing model endpoints or to a read-only mode? We need to know how failback impacts downstream queues.

Fallback plan: automatic fallback will route to your existing model endpoints (we perform a graceful redirect). We will NOT default to read-only; instead, traffic is split and, on trigger, we route 100% back to your current endpoints. That transition includes a KV cache flush and 2-minute quiesce window to avoid duplicate requests. We've summarized failure semantics in redwood-canary-checklist.pdf (see section 3).

> 3) Security artifacts: security@hearthwave.com asked for: SOC 2 Type II scope, retention and delete-by-request flow, and an on-prem dataflow diagram. Do you have a one-page summary or link we can share with them?

Evelyn — I attached a one-page security summary and a link to our SOC 2 package in the related_links above for their review. If Hearthwave needs a deeper walkthrough, we can set a short call with our Security team next week.

Next steps / Proposed schedule:
- Tue Nov 16: Pilot environment provisioned (Redwood infra team).
- Fri Nov 19 01:00–04:00 UTC: Canary window #1 (traffic slice 5% -> monitor 48h).
- Sun Nov 21 02:00–05:00 UTC: Production cutover window (contingent on canary acceptance).
- Training: engineers Nov 12 & 13 (90-min remote sessions), ops runbook Nov 17 (60-min).

Please confirm the training attendee list and which slot you prefer for the final cutover. Once you confirm, procurement can sign the implementation SOW and we’ll lock the provisioning dates.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Daniel —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and great questions. Confirming the schedule Karthik proposed; we’ll provision the pilot on Nov 16 and run the first canary on Nov 19. I’ll own the go/no-go checklist during the canary and will send the acceptance form 24 hours before the production cutover.

Proposed gating for go/no-go call:
- Functional acceptance (integration tests pass)
- Performance SLOs met (P95 latency < 250ms, error rate < 0.5%)
- No open Sev2/Sev1 issues in the last 12 hours

If those three are green, we’ll proceed with the Sun Nov 21 production cutover. I’ll schedule a 30-minute go/no-go sync for Sun Nov 21 01:00 UTC to finalize — if that time conflicts let me know and we’ll adjust.

Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
